content.what_it_is: Interactive Python frame renderer for vessel-island eta outputs. It builds fixed Users/Gaby paths, loads eta_00001 and depth, reads start/end frame numbers, constructs coordinates from depth dimensions (L8-L29), then renders each frame in range(ns,ne), masks eta above 10, derives a displayed time as (num-1)*2.5 formatted as an integer, and saves one PNG per frame (L35-L61).

io.name: fdep concatenated with depth.txt via numpy.loadtxt

calls: os.path.join at L10-L11, L13, and L39
np.loadtxt at L14, L20, and L40
np.asarray, float, and range at L28-L29
unresolved: Definite path-concatenation defect at L11 and L20: fdep has no trailing separator, so fdep+'depth.txt' produces a path ending in 'vessel_island_beachdepth.txt' rather than a depth.txt child and normally fails before plotting.

The path components at L10-L11 start with 'Users' rather than '/Users' (or a drive/root), so despite appearing workstation-specific they are relative to the current directory; the user-path instruction does not match the constructed paths.
End-bound off-by-one at L17-L18 and L35: an input described as the plot end number is excluded by range(ns,ne), so frame ne is never rendered; ns==ne renders nothing.
Numerical formatting defect at L53-L55: (num-1)*2.5 can be half-integral, but %.4d truncates it to an integer (for example 2.5 becomes 0002), producing incorrect displayed seconds.
mask loaded from eta_00001 at L13-L14 is never used; eta masking instead relies only on eta>10 at L42.
No dy exists and y at L29 reuses dx, forcing square spacing; eta dimensions are also not checked against dep-derived x/y before L44.
Matplotlib pcolor at L44 does not specify shading while coordinate lengths match eta dimensions, making edge coverage version-dependent.
